Issue 07:
# 07 — Stripe payment + webhook + ThankYou

Status: needs-triage
Type: AFK

## What to build

Complete the payment flow end-to-end: mount the Stripe PaymentElement using the `clientSecret` from issue 06, handle payment confirmation, build the `fulfill-order` webhook Edge Function that flips the order to `payment_confirmed`, and build the ThankYou page that polls for that status. After this slice a shopper can pay with a test card and see a confirmed order.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Stripe `PaymentElement` mounts on the checkout page after `clientSecret` is received
- [ ] Successful payment redirects to `/thank-you?payment_intent=pi_xxx`
- [ ] `fulfill-order` Edge Function verifies the `Stripe-Signature` header; returns 400 on invalid/missing signature
- [ ] `fulfill-order` updates the matching `orders` row to `status: payment_confirmed` on `payment_intent.succeeded`
- [ ] `fulfill-order` returns 200 and does nothing for unrecognised event types
- [ ] `fulfill-order` is idempotent — processing the same event twice does not corrupt the order
- [ ] `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` configured in Supabase Edge Function environment
- [ ] ThankYou page polls Supabase every 2 seconds for `stripe_payment_id = pi_xxx AND status = payment_confirmed`
- [ ] ThankYou page displays order confirmation when `payment_confirmed` is detected
- [ ] ThankYou page stops polling after receiving `payment_confirmed`
- [ ] ThankYou page displays a fallback message after 30 seconds without confirmation
- [ ] Full flow verified with Stripe test card `4242 4242 4242 4242`
- [ ] Tests: `fulfill-order` webhook behaviours, ThankYou page polling + timeout

## Blocked by

- 06 — Checkout form + create-payment-intent

Issue 08:
# 08 — Admin auth + route protection

Status: needs-triage
Type: AFK

## What to build

Build the login page and the `AdminRoute` wrapper that protects all `/admin/*` routes. After this slice the artist can log in with email and password, and any unauthenticated or non-admin attempt to access admin URLs is redirected to `/login`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `LoginPage` has email and password fields and a submit button
- [ ] Successful login with a valid admin account redirects to `/admin/orders`
- [ ] Failed login shows a clear error message
- [ ] `AdminRoute` wrapper checks Supabase session on mount
- [ ] `AdminRoute` shows a loading state while the session check is in progress
- [ ] `AdminRoute` redirects to `/login` when no session exists
- [ ] `AdminRoute` redirects to `/login` when session exists but `profiles.is_admin = false`
- [ ] `AdminRoute` renders children when session exists and `is_admin = true`
- [ ] All `/admin/*` routes are wrapped with `AdminRoute`
- [ ] Shared admin nav links to `/admin/orders`, `/admin/products`, `/admin/banners`
- [ ] Tests: all four `AdminRoute` states (loading, no session, non-admin session, admin session)

## Blocked by

- 01 — Supabase schema + project config
- 02 — React scaffold + routing skeleton

plan.sprint_goal: Complete the Stripe payment end-to-end flow (PaymentElement → webhook → ThankYou polling) and lock down all admin routes behind session + is_admin checks

dev1.task: 1) In src/pages/Checkout.jsx: after receiving clientSecret from the create-payment-intent Edge Function, mount Stripe PaymentElement using @stripe/react-stripe-js Elements provider with the clientSecret, wire the confirmPayment call to redirect to /thank-you?payment_intent={pi.id} on success. 2) In src/pages/ThankYou.jsx: read payment_intent query param from URL, poll Supabase orders table every 2 seconds for a row where stripe_payment_id = param AND status = 'payment_confirmed', show a loading/polling state on mount, render order confirmation (customer name, items summary) when confirmed, stop polling on confirmation, and show a fallback message after 30 seconds without confirmation. 3) Write tests for ThankYou page covering: initial polling state, confirmation displayed when payment_confirmed returned, fallback shown after 30s timeout, polling stops after confirmation, polling stops after timeout. 4) In src/pages/Login.jsx: wire up the existing form to supabase.auth.signInWithPassword, redirect to /admin/orders on success, display error message on failure. 5) In src/components/AdminRoute.jsx: implement session check via supabase.auth.getSession on mount, fetch profiles row for is_admin flag, show loading spinner while checking, redirect to /login if no session or is_admin = false, render children if is_admin = true. Write tests for all four AdminRoute states (loading, no session, non-admin, admin). 6) Confirm all /admin/* routes in src/App.jsx are wrapped with AdminRoute.
dev1.context_needed: Checkout.jsx already exists and calls create-payment-intent — it receives clientSecret. CartContext items shape: [{ id, name, price (cents), image_url, quantity }]. supabase.js exports a configured Supabase client. stripe.js exports the loadStripe promise (use VITE_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY). orders table has columns: id, stripe_payment_id TEXT, status TEXT, customer_name TEXT, customer_email TEXT, total INTEGER. profiles table has columns: id (matches auth.uid()), is_admin BOOLEAN. RLS on orders: public SELECT allowed (needed for ThankYou polling without auth). RLS on profiles: users can SELECT their own row only. App.jsx already has routing skeleton with /admin/* routes and AdminRoute component stub.

dev2.task: Build the fulfill-order Supabase Edge Function at supabase/functions/fulfill-order/index.ts. It must: 1) Read the raw request body and Stripe-Signature header. 2) Verify the webhook signature using Stripe's constructEvent with STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET from env — return HTTP 400 if signature is invalid or missing. 3) On event type payment_intent.succeeded, extract payment_intent id from event.data.object.id, then UPDATE orders SET status = 'payment_confirmed' WHERE stripe_payment_id = pi_id AND status != 'payment_confirmed' (idempotency guard — do not overwrite if already confirmed). 4) Return HTTP 200 for all unrecognised event types without touching the DB. 5) Write tests in supabase/functions/fulfill-order/index.test.ts covering: invalid/missing Stripe-Signature returns 400, payment_intent.succeeded updates order to payment_confirmed, unrecognised event type returns 200 and makes no DB change, idempotent — second call with same event does not corrupt order. 6) Document the required STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET env var in a README comment or supabase/functions/fulfill-order/README.md so it can be configured in the Supabase dashboard.
dev2.context_needed: Existing create-payment-intent/index.ts for reference on how Edge Functions are structured in this project (Deno runtime, stripe npm import via esm.sh or npm: specifier, supabase service role client init). orders table schema: id UUID, stripe_payment_id TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT (values: order_received, payment_confirmed, order_confirmed, sent, cancelled), customer_name, customer_email, shipping_*, total INTEGER cents. Service role key is available as SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY env var in Edge Function runtime. Stripe signature verification requires raw body bytes — do not parse body as JSON before verification. create-payment-intent/index.test.ts for test patterns (mock shapes for Supabase client and Stripe).

plan.shared_types: Order status enum (use as string literals): 'order_received' | 'payment_confirmed' | 'order_confirmed' | 'sent' | 'cancelled'. ThankYou polling query shape — Supabase SELECT returns: { id: string, stripe_payment_id: string, status: string, customer_name: string, total: number }. Webhook payload shape Dev2 produces and Dev1 polls for must both treat stripe_payment_id as the join key between Stripe PI id and the orders row.

# fulfill-order Edge Function

Handles Stripe webhook events to update order status after payment.

## Required Environment Variables

Configure these in the Supabase Dashboard under
**Project Settings → Edge Functions → Secrets** (or via `supabase secrets set`):

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | The webhook signing secret from your Stripe Dashboard webhook endpoint (starts with `whsec_`). **Required.** Without this the function will reject every request with HTTP 400. |
| `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` | Your Stripe secret API key (starts with `sk_live_` or `sk_test_`). |
| `SUPABASE_URL` | Injected automatically by the Supabase runtime. |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | Injected automatically by the Supabase runtime. Grants the function permission to call the `confirm_order_payment` RPC. |

## Stripe Dashboard Setup

1. Go to **Developers → Webhooks → Add endpoint**.
2. Set the endpoint URL to `https://<project-ref>.functions.supabase.co/fulfill-order`.
3. Select the `payment_intent.succeeded` event.
4. Copy the **Signing secret** and save it as `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

## Database RPC Dependency

This function calls `confirm_order_payment(p_stripe_payment_id TEXT)` which must
exist in the database. The RPC updates the order row:

```sql
-- supabase/migrations/YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_confirm_order_payment_rpc.sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION confirm_order_payment(p_stripe_payment_id TEXT)
RETURNS void
LANGUAGE sql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
  UPDATE orders
  SET status = 'payment_confirmed'
  WHERE stripe_payment_id = p_stripe_payment_id
    -- Idempotency guard: do not overwrite if already confirmed
    AND status != 'payment_confirmed';
$$;
```

## Event Handling

| Event type | Action |
|---|---|
| `payment_intent.succeeded` | Calls `confirm_order_payment` RPC; returns HTTP 200. |
| Any other type | Returns HTTP 200 immediately; no DB change. |

Returning HTTP 200 for unrecognised events prevents Stripe from retrying them
endlessly. Returning HTTP 500 on DB failure signals Stripe to retry delivery.
